display.purpose: Rare. Page-level identity and empty-state headlines only.

headline.purpose: Page titles and primary metric values.

body.purpose: The default for everything meant to be read.

label.purpose: Field labels, table cells, badges, metadata, navigation. The dominant size in this interface.

shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: Step 0. Page ground, rows, inline groups, table headers. The default.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Step 1. A card resting on the page. The only shadow implemented today.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Step 3. Dialogs and the operation overlay. There is no step 4.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for colour and state transitions.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover and focus feedback on controls.

motion.name: no-bounce
motion.purpose: Bounce and elastic easing are banned; this is instrumentation, not a toy.

motion.name: no-pulse
motion.purpose: A pulse implies live data. Static status must never pretend to be live.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single call to action on a view. Everything else is secondary or danger.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; background: rgb(var(--primary)); color: rgb(var(--primary-fg)); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-lg); padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgb(var(--primary-hover)); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgb(var(--primary) / 0.3); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button. Any action that is not the one primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; background: rgb(var(--surface)); color: rgb(var(--fg)); border: 1px solid rgb(var(--border-strong)); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgb(var(--surface-2)); }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive actions. Serious, not shouting: outlined rather than a filled red block, so it reads as consequential only once considered.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; background: rgb(var(--surface)); color: rgb(var(--danger)); border: 1px solid rgb(var(--border-strong)); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms, border-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: rgb(var(--danger) / 0.1); border-color: rgb(var(--danger) / 0.4); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The unit of page composition. One subject per card. Cards never nest; internal grouping uses a hairline row.
components.css: .ds-card { background: rgb(var(--surface)); border: 1px solid rgb(var(--border)); border-radius: var(--radius-xl); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.04), 0 1px 3px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.06); } .ds-card-header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; border-bottom: 1px solid rgb(var(--border)); padding: 0.75rem 1rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: rgb(var(--fg)); } .ds-card-body { padding: 1rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; color: rgb(var(--fg-muted)); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Focus is border plus a 2px ring. The ring is the accessible focus indicator and must never be removed.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: rgb(var(--surface)); color: rgb(var(--fg)); border: 1px solid rgb(var(--border-strong)); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.25rem; outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgb(var(--fg-subtle)); } .ds-input:focus { border-color: rgb(var(--primary)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgb(var(--primary) / 0.3); }

components.name: Status Dot
components.description: Healthy is green; inactive is subtle grey. Never red for merely 'off' — a service that is supposed to be stopped is not a fault. Never animated.
components.css: .ds-dot { display: inline-block; width: 0.5rem; height: 0.5rem; border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-dot-ok { background: rgb(var(--success)); } .ds-dot-off { background: rgb(var(--fg-subtle)); }

components.name: Usage Bar
components.description: Crosses from primary to warning at 75% and to danger at 90%. The thresholds are part of the component's meaning, not a per-instance choice.
components.css: .ds-usage { height: 0.5rem; width: 100%; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgb(var(--surface-2)); } .ds-usage-fill { height: 100%; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgb(var(--warning)); transition: width 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); }

components.name: Sidebar Item
components.description: The rail is a dark slate in both themes; navigation is chrome and the content area is the work.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; color: rgb(var(--sidebar-fg)); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: rgb(var(--sidebar-hover)); } .ds-nav-active { background: rgb(var(--sidebar-active)); color: rgb(var(--sidebar-active-fg)); }

narrative.overview:
A control tower is quiet most of the night. Its whole design exists so that when something does happen, nobody has to look for it. That ordering governs every conflict in this system: at rest be calm, in use be dense and exact, on exception be unmissable. Calm is not decoration — it is what makes an alarm legible. If everything is loud, nothing is.

This is a professional tool operated in long sessions on wide screens. Information density outranks whitespace, and restraint in components buys room for data. The panel is instrumentation, not furniture and not a brochure.

The third rule is the one that earns the metaphor. This product's documented history is of operations that stop halfway and interfaces that cannot say so. A design that cannot express 'this is stuck, here is why, here is your way out' is not finished, however elegant its steady state.
keyCharacteristics: Quiet at rest, dense in use, unmissable on exception
A 12-14px interface: 854 of 929 size declarations are label or body
Semantic colour is reserved for system state and never used decoratively
Depth is tonal first, shadow second; four elevation steps and no more
One shell for four roles, rendered from capabilities rather than per-role layouts
A service that is not installed is invisible: no empty screens, no disabled menus

rules.name: Semantic colour means something
rules.body: success, warning and danger carry meaning and must never be used decoratively. When they appear, the operator is entitled to conclude something is true about the system.

rules.name: Twelve is the floor
rules.body: 12px is the smallest step and nothing goes below it. The next request for 'one size smaller' is answered with weight, colour, or spacing instead.

rules.name: Weight carries hierarchy, size does not
rules.body: Because the size range is deliberately narrow, weight and colour do the hierarchical work. A screen that needs a new size step almost always needs better grouping.

rules.name: Tonal before shadow
rules.body: Depth comes from surface, surface-2, surface-3 and borders. Shadow marks only what genuinely floats. In dark mode shadows barely read: step up a surface tone rather than increasing opacity.

rules.name: Concentric corners
rules.body: The bigger the box, the rounder the corner: lg for controls, xl for the card holding them, 2xl for the dialog holding the card.

rules.name: Operation states are designed, not incidental
rules.body: Every privileged operation renders stage, elapsed time, request id, and on failure the exact error code plus one action. Four designed states are required: running, succeeded, failed-with-cause, unreachable-backend. The last is not a spinner.

rules.name: Contrast is a requirement
rules.body: WCAG 2.1 AA is the target. fg-subtle is a placeholder and disabled colour only, never the colour of information.

dos: Do reference semantic tokens (bg-surface, text-fg-muted, border-border) and let theme and skin layers resolve them.
Do reserve success / warning / danger for actual system state.
Do use weight and colour before reaching for a new size step.
Do give every long-running operation a terminal state and an exit.
Do set tabular-nums on digits that align in a column.
Do keep the whole page keyboard-operable with a visible focus ring.
donts: Don't hard-code a hex colour, font family, or radius.
Don't put a thick or one-sided accent border on a card.
Don't nest a card inside a card.
Don't introduce a size step below 12px or a fifth elevation step.
Don't use a coloured glow, a gradient background, or a pulsing dot.
Don't use danger to mean 'off', or fg-subtle to carry information.
Don't add a decorative icon tile above a heading or an uppercase eyebrow above every card title.
Don't design for or against the competitor skins while that decision is open.
